sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
I added this row to `budget.csv`:

```
groceries,600,keep under $600/month; flag anything that would push it over
```

I set the limit to 600, since the file stores monthly caps. You said "under $600", so treat $600 as the ceiling. I'll flag any grocery spending that would take the month past it.

The CSV can't enforce the flag. If you want automatic checking, you could add a spending log that I compare against this limit.

actions.command: ls; cat budget.csv groceries.csv meal-plan.md 2>&1 | head -50

cat > groceries.csv <<'EOF'
item,cost_usd
Rice and grains (bulk),25.00
Pasta and noodles,18.00
Canned beans and tomatoes,22.00
Bread and tortillas,20.00
Oats and cereal,15.00
Chicken (thighs and breasts),48.00
Ground turkey/beef,36.00
Fish (salmon, canned tuna),40.00
Eggs (4 dozen),20.00
Milk and yogurt,34.00
Cheese,22.00
Fresh vegetables,70.00
Fresh fruit,55.00
Frozen vegetables and fruit,24.00
Potatoes and onions,16.00
Cooking oil, spices, sauces,28.00
Coffee and tea,24.00
Snacks,25.00
Household staples (non-food) ,30.00
Buffer for price changes,25.00
EOF
awk -F, 'NR>1{s+=$NF}END{print s}' groceries.csv

cat > meal-plan.md <<'EOF'
# Meal plan: December 2026

Grocery list: see `groceries.csv`.

## Budget
- Planned total: **$597.00**
- Limit (from `budget.csv`): $600/month
- Remaining: **$3.00**. This is under budget, but the margin is very thin.

**Flag:** Any additions would push the month over $600. If you add something, cut an item of equal cost. The easiest places to cut are snacks ($25), the price-change buffer ($25), and fresh fruit ($55).

## Staples (bought once, used all month)
Rice, pasta, canned goods, oats, oil and spices, coffee and tea.

## Weekly rotation
- **Breakfasts:** oats or cereal with fruit and yogurt, or eggs on toast.
- **Lunches:** tortilla wraps, or rice bowls with beans and vegetables.
- **Dinners:**
  - Week 1: chicken stir-fry with rice
  - Week 2: pasta with turkey/beef tomato sauce
  - Week 3: baked salmon, potatoes and roasted vegetables
  - Week 4: bean and vegetable chili with rice, plus a leftovers night

## Notes
- Buy the chicken, meat and fish in bulk and freeze them in portions.
- Prices are estimates. Check them against actual receipts and adjust.
- Eating out has its own $150 budget and isn't included here.
EOF

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I created `groceries.csv` with 20 items and wrote the summary in `meal-plan.md`. The plan comes to $597.00, which is $3 under your $600 grocery limit in `budget.csv`.

The prices are my own estimates, not figures from your receipts, so check them against what you actually pay. The list also includes $30 of non-food household staples and a $25 buffer for price changes.

Because the margin is so thin, I flagged in `meal-plan.md` that any addition would put you over $600. It suggests cutting snacks ($25), the buffer ($25) or fresh fruit ($55) to make room.

The plan itself has a four-week dinner rotation and notes on buying meat in bulk and freezing it. I titled it "December 2026", since today is Nov 22.
